purpose: Source-backed candidate events for currently open dates. These are ready for later integration after the scalable TRMNL runtime feed is in place, so they do not increase the current TRMNL polling payload.

candidates.title: Burj Khalifa opens at skyscraper scale
candidates.summary: The formal opening of Burj Khalifa marked completion of an 828-metre supertall tower whose buttressed-core structure, high-strength concrete and staged vertical construction pushed skyscraper engineering upward.
candidates.lesson: Extreme height is a system problem: structure, wind response, concrete pumping, vertical transport and construction logistics all have to scale together.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms the formal opening on Jan. 4, 2010 and describes construction/structural details.

candidates.title: Painter patents the crown bottle cap
candidates.summary: William Painter received a U.S. patent for a bottle-sealing device: a cheap crimped metal cap that could hold pressure and seal carbonated drinks reliably.
candidates.lesson: Packaging is engineering. A small closure can reshape an industry when it solves sealing, cost, hygiene and repeatable application at the same time.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Patent record confirms Feb. 2, 1892 and describes the metallic sealing cap/bottle-sealing device.

candidates.title: Deep Blue wins one game against Kasparov
candidates.summary: IBM's Deep Blue won the first game of its Philadelphia match against world chess champion Garry Kasparov, the first victory by a computer against a reigning champion under regular time controls.
candidates.lesson: A milestone does not have to be the final victory. A narrow win can prove that architecture, compute power and search strategy have crossed a meaningful threshold.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. IBM source confirms the February 1996 match, Deep Blue's first-game win and the first victory by a computer against a reigning world champion under regular time controls.

candidates.title: Westland/Hallmark recalls 143 million pounds of beef
candidates.summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture announced the recall of about 143 million pounds of beef after animal-handling violations and inspection-control failures at Westland/Hallmark became public.
candidates.lesson: Food production safety depends on enforceable process controls and traceability; inspection that cannot see the real process becomes paperwork, not protection.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Useful underrepresented category candidate; source supports the recall scale and inspection-control concerns.

candidates.title: Trevithick's locomotive hauls iron on rails
candidates.summary: Richard Trevithick's Penydarren locomotive hauled iron and passengers along a South Wales tramroad, demonstrating that steam power could move heavy loads on rails.
candidates.lesson: A breakthrough can arrive before the supporting infrastructure is ready; vehicle, track strength, load and operating economics all have to mature together.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Museum Wales confirms Feb. 21, 1804 and the world's first railway journey from Penydarren to the Merthyr-Cardiff Canal.

candidates.title: Castle Bravo produces far more fallout than expected
candidates.summary: The Castle Bravo thermonuclear test produced a roughly 15-megaton yield, far above its expected yield, spreading radioactive fallout across Marshall Islands communities, U.S. personnel and a Japanese fishing vessel.
candidates.lesson: A model error in a high-energy system can become a public disaster; uncertainty, exclusion zones and environmental pathways must be sized for what could happen, not only what is expected.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms Mar. 1, 1954, the 15 Mt yield, lower estimate, fallout and affected populations.

candidates.title: Forth Bridge opens as a steel cantilever landmark
candidates.summary: The Forth Bridge was formally opened by the Prince of Wales after testing and inspection, joining the railway across the Firth of Forth with a massive steel cantilever structure.
candidates.lesson: A landmark structure needs more than a bold form. Load testing, inspection, erection sequence, materials and operating purpose all have to meet before opening day.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Network Rail confirms the formal opening on Mar. 4, 1890 and describes the bridge, testing and final rivet ceremony.

candidates.title: Bell receives the telephone patent
candidates.summary: Alexander Graham Bell received U.S. Patent No. 174,465 for transmitting vocal or other sounds telegraphically, giving the telephone a defensible technical and legal starting point.
candidates.lesson: A communications breakthrough needs more than a clever device; it needs a reproducible signal path, a defined interface and a claim precise enough to build around.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. National Archives record supports the Mar. 7, 1876 patent drawing/oath date.

candidates.title: Vanguard 1 proves solar power in orbit
candidates.summary: Vanguard 1 launched as the world's first solar-powered satellite, testing a three-stage launch vehicle and long-lived spacecraft systems in Earth orbit.
candidates.lesson: A small spacecraft can become a durable experiment when power, telemetry, orbit and environmental exposure are designed as one long-running system.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NASA source confirms Mar. 17, 1958 launch and first solar-powered satellite claim.

candidates.title: Benz puts a motor bus into regular service
candidates.summary: The world's first motor-powered omnibus entered service between Siegen, Netphen and Deuz, turning the motor vehicle from a private machine into shared transport infrastructure.
candidates.lesson: A vehicle becomes public infrastructure only when engine reliability, route length, capacity, maintenance and operating economics work together.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Mercedes-Benz Public Archive confirms 18 March 1895 and the Siegen-Netphen-Deuz service.

candidates.title: Sydney Harbour Bridge opens as a steel arch landmark
candidates.summary: Sydney Harbour Bridge opened after a major steel-arch construction effort, joining road, rail and pedestrian traffic across the harbour as a national infrastructure milestone.
candidates.lesson: A landmark bridge is more than a span; fabrication, erection sequence, transport demand and public operations must meet at the same opening day.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source supports the Mar. 19, 1932 opening and bridge significance; useful civil breakthrough candidate.

candidates.title: Browns Ferry turns a cable fire into a nuclear safety lesson
candidates.summary: A fire at the Browns Ferry nuclear plant damaged safety-related electrical cables and became a major driver of U.S. nuclear fire-protection regulation.
candidates.lesson: Separation only works when physical routing, barriers, detection and response are independent enough that one fire cannot remove redundant safety functions together.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NRC source documents the Browns Ferry Nuclear Plant Fire of 1975 and its role in the history of NRC fire regulations; later promotion should use one of the linked NRC reports for finer event details.

candidates.title: A second Comet breakup confirms a fatigue crisis
candidates.summary: South African Airways Flight 201, a de Havilland Comet operated through BOAC, broke up after departing Rome. Together with the earlier Elba crash, the accident exposed fatigue failure in pressurized jetliner cabins.
candidates.lesson: Pressurization turns every flight into a load cycle. Full-scale fatigue testing, manufacturing detail and inspection must match the real structure, not an idealized section.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. FAA Lessons Learned page explicitly covers the Apr. 8, 1954 Naples crash and links the Comet accidents to pressure-cabin fatigue failure.

candidates.title: Hunt patents a safer spring pin
candidates.summary: Walter Hunt received a U.S. patent for a dress pin with a spring and clasp, turning bent wire into a cheap, repeatable fastening mechanism that protected the point.
candidates.lesson: Good product engineering can be tiny: store elastic energy, guide motion and shield the hazard with as few parts as possible.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Patent record confirms Apr. 10, 1849 and describes Hunt's dress-pin mechanism.

candidates.title: Apollo 13 loses an oxygen tank on the way to the Moon
candidates.summary: An oxygen tank ruptured in Apollo 13's service module, draining power and life-support resources and forcing the crew to use the lunar module as a lifeboat.
candidates.lesson: Shared resources create shared failure modes; power, oxygen, cooling, controls and emergency procedures must be tested as one survival system.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NASA source supports Apr. 13, 1970, oxygen tank rupture, power loss and mission abort.

candidates.title: Titanic's iceberg strike defeats compartment safety
candidates.summary: RMS Titanic struck an iceberg late on 14 April. Flooding across multiple watertight compartments exceeded the ship's survivability assumptions, and the liner sank early the next morning.
candidates.lesson: Compartmentalization only protects against the damage case it actually bounds; collision energy, breach length, flooding paths and evacuation capacity must be considered together.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source supports the Apr. 14 iceberg strike and flooding/sinking sequence with engineering framing.

candidates.title: San Francisco burns after the earthquake
candidates.summary: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake caused severe shaking damage, but the ensuing fires drove much of the catastrophe and made the event a lasting urban fire-safety lesson.
candidates.lesson: A city is coupled infrastructure. Gas, water, streets, communications, firefighting access and building stock can turn one hazard into a second, larger failure mode.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. USGS source confirms Apr. 18, 1906 and describes the earthquake and fire death/destruction context.

candidates.title: Game Boy makes portable gaming durable
candidates.summary: Nintendo released the Game Boy in Japan, pairing modest hardware with cartridge software, long battery life and a portable form that made handheld gaming a mass-market platform.
candidates.lesson: Consumer hardware can win by optimizing the whole use case: battery life, cost, durability, controls, software library and pocketable design can matter more than peak specs.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms Japan release on Apr. 21, 1989 and describes the handheld console, cartridge system and development context.

candidates.title: Deepwater Horizon sinks after the Macondo blowout
candidates.summary: Two days after the blowout and explosion that killed 11 workers, the Deepwater Horizon drilling rig sank in about 5,000 feet of water in the Gulf of Mexico.
candidates.lesson: A well-control failure is a system failure: barriers, test interpretation, alarms, emergency disconnects and evacuation all have to work before hydrocarbons reach ignition.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NOAA timeline confirms Apr. 22, 2010 rig sinking after the Apr. 20 explosion.

candidates.title: Sunshine Mine fire exposes underground evacuation limits
candidates.summary: A fire in Idaho's Sunshine Mine killed 91 miners, most by smoke inhalation, and became a major case in mine-fire investigation, warning, escape and respiratory protection.
candidates.lesson: Underground safety depends on time: detection, communication, refuge, breathing equipment and escape routes must work before smoke and toxic gases own the only paths out.
candidates.source_label: U.S. Bureau of Mines via Mining History Association
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source republishes the U.S. Bureau of Mines investigation of the Sunshine Mine fire disaster of May 2, 1972; later pass should cite the original report if a stable federal copy is found.

candidates.title: WHO declares smallpox eradicated
candidates.summary: The 33rd World Health Assembly officially declared the world free of smallpox, closing a global vaccination and surveillance campaign against a disease that had killed hundreds of millions.
candidates.lesson: Public-health engineering is still systems engineering: vaccine production, cold chains, surveillance, reporting and local execution all have to close the loop.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. WHO source confirms May 8, 1980 declaration by the 33rd World Health Assembly and the global eradication context.

candidates.title: Zuse completes the program-controlled Z3
candidates.summary: Konrad Zuse completed the Z3, a program-controlled electromechanical digital computer that used relay logic to automate calculations before electronic computers became practical.
candidates.lesson: A computing breakthrough can come from architecture before speed: representation, programmability and repeatable control define the machine.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms May 12, 1941 and describes the Z3 as the first program-controlled electromechanical digital computer.

candidates.title: Takata acknowledges a national airbag recall
candidates.summary: Takata acknowledged that defective airbag inflators required a national recall. The defect could make inflators rupture and spray fragments into the passenger compartment.
candidates.lesson: A safety device becomes a hazard when propellant chemistry, aging, humidity exposure and quality control are not validated across the real service environment.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Strong automotive failure candidate with an official DOT source.

candidates.title: Davis and Strauss patent riveted workwear
candidates.summary: Jacob Davis and Levi Strauss received a U.S. patent for reinforcing garment stress points with metal rivets, turning durable work trousers into a repeatable manufactured product.
candidates.lesson: A small fastening detail can become a manufacturing breakthrough when it solves the common failure point and can be applied consistently at scale.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Good low-overlap manufacturing example with a primary-record-oriented source.

candidates.title: Hoover Dam receives its last concrete
candidates.summary: The last concrete was placed in Hoover Dam after a massive staged pour, cooling-pipe and construction-logistics effort for one of the era's defining infrastructure projects.
candidates.lesson: Mass concrete is a thermal and logistics problem as much as a structural one; sequence, cooling, placement rate and quality control decide whether scale stays sound.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Bureau of Reclamation source confirms first concrete on Jun. 6, 1933, last concrete on May 29, 1935 and peak placement figures.

candidates.title: South Fork Dam fails above Johnstown
candidates.summary: The South Fork Dam failed after modifications, blocked drainage and heavy rain left the reservoir overtopping. The resulting flood devastated Johnstown and killed more than two thousand people.
candidates.lesson: A dam is never just earthwork; spillways, outlets, maintenance, ownership and emergency warning are part of the safety system.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms May 31, 1889, dam failure, water volume and deaths; strong civil failure candidate.

candidates.title: Surveyor 1 soft-lands on the Moon
candidates.summary: NASA's Surveyor 1 landed successfully on the Moon's Ocean of Storms, returning images and surface data that helped prove automated lunar landing technology before Apollo.
candidates.lesson: A precursor mission earns its keep when it reduces uncertainty for the next system: landing dynamics, surface bearing, telemetry and operations all become measured facts.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NASA confirms Surveyor 1's Jun. 2, 1966 soft landing, first American Moon soft landing and return of thousands of images.

candidates.title: Le Mans crash sends racing debris into spectators
candidates.summary: During the 24 Hours of Le Mans, a high-speed collision sent a racing car and debris into spectator areas, killing more than 80 people and exposing how track layout, barriers and vehicle energy interact.
candidates.lesson: Spectators are part of the safety envelope. Speed, stopping zones, debris paths, fuel, materials and crowd separation must be designed as one system.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. AP supports Jun. 11, 1955 and the more-than-80 death toll; needs later source-quality pass for detailed vehicle/track/material mechanisms.

candidates.title: Goodyear patents vulcanized rubber
candidates.summary: Charles Goodyear received a U.S. patent for treating rubber with heat and sulfur, creating a more stable material that could keep useful properties across changing temperatures.
candidates.lesson: A material becomes broadly useful when processing controls its behavior in the actual environment, not just under ideal shop conditions.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Strong materials breakthrough; source is the patent record.

candidates.title: Kwolek's aramid patent points toward Kevlar
candidates.summary: Stephanie Kwolek received a U.S. patent for processing aromatic polyamides into strong fibers, part of the technical path that led to Kevlar and other high-strength aramid materials.
candidates.lesson: Materials innovation often hides in process windows: chemistry, solvent behavior and fiber formation determine whether strength can be manufactured.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Good underrepresented materials entry; may deserve a later source-quality pass against DuPont or ACS material if used.

candidates.title: Sholes, Glidden and Soule patent the typewriter
candidates.summary: Christopher Latham Sholes, Carlos Glidden and Samuel W. Soule received a U.S. patent for improvements in type-writing machines, helping move writing from handcraft toward repeatable office machinery.
candidates.lesson: An interface becomes infrastructure when mechanics, input layout, carriage motion and manufacturable parts make repeated human work faster and more consistent.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Patent record confirms Jun. 23, 1868 and the type-writing machine invention.

candidates.title: Barclays unveils the first cash machine
candidates.summary: Barclays opened an automated teller machine at its Enfield branch, giving customers a way to withdraw cash directly from a machine outside normal counter service.
candidates.lesson: A useful consumer system hides complexity: authentication, dispensing, accounting, physical security and user trust all have to work in one small public interface.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Historic England confirms the Enfield bank was the first in the world fitted with an ATM and that its official opening was on Jun. 27, 1967.

candidates.title: Sampoong department store collapses from structural neglect
candidates.summary: The Sampoong Department Store in Seoul collapsed after unsafe structural changes and overloading contributed to punching-shear failure in the building's flat-slab system.
candidates.lesson: A building use change is an engineering change. Columns, slab capacity, added loads, vibration and visible cracking must trigger analysis and evacuation authority.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Journal abstract supports Jun. 29, 1995 and collapse-cause inspection; needs later source-quality pass before promotion because full details are behind abstract/paywall.

candidates.title: Dolly proves adult-cell cloning can work
candidates.summary: Dolly was born at the Roslin Institute after being cloned from an adult mammary-gland cell, proving that a specialized adult cell could be reprogrammed to develop into a whole organism.
candidates.lesson: Biological engineering depends on process control at tiny interfaces: cell source, nuclear transfer, embryo development and surrogate timing all have to align.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms Jul. 5, 1996 birth and first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

candidates.title: Mont-Blanc Tunnel opens beneath the Alps
candidates.summary: The Mont-Blanc Tunnel was inaugurated by the French and Italian presidents, linking Chamonix and Courmayeur through a road tunnel beneath the mountain.
candidates.lesson: A tunnel is a complete operating system. Alignment, ventilation, excavation, border operations, traffic flow and emergency response matter as much as the bore itself.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Official tunnel history confirms the Jul. 16, 1965 inauguration by Presidents Giuseppe Saragat and Charles de Gaulle.

candidates.title: Eastland capsizes while still tied to the dock
candidates.summary: The passenger steamer Eastland rolled over in the Chicago River before departing, with more than 2,500 passengers and crew aboard and 844 people killed.
candidates.lesson: Stability is a loading condition, not a paperwork certificate. Passenger distribution, ballast, freeboard and last-minute modifications can erase reserve stability at the pier.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms Jul. 24, 1915, capsize at the wharf, more than 2,500 aboard and 844 deaths; later pass should use an official investigation source if a stable one is found.

candidates.title: Delta 191 reveals the danger of microbursts
candidates.summary: Delta Air Lines Flight 191 crashed on approach to Dallas/Fort Worth after encountering intense wind shear from a thunderstorm downdraft, highlighting a poorly understood low-altitude weather hazard.
candidates.lesson: Aircraft safety depends on sensing the environment in time; training, weather radar, warning systems and go-around decisions must match the hazard's speed.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms Aug. 2, 1985, DFW crash and NTSB wind-shear/microburst finding.

candidates.title: Banqiao Dam fails in a cascade of flooding
candidates.summary: China's Banqiao Dam failed during extreme rainfall from Typhoon Nina, releasing a destructive flood and contributing to a wider cascade of dam failures downstream.
candidates.lesson: Reservoir safety depends on the whole flood system: hydrology, spillway capacity, gate operation, communications and downstream emergency planning must survive the same storm.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. IChemE article confirms Aug. 8, 1975, Banqiao failure, flood wave and downstream cascade; later pass should seek a stronger primary/official engineering source before promotion.

candidates.title: Firestone recalls millions of tires after tread separations
candidates.summary: Bridgestone/Firestone announced a large recall of ATX, ATX II and Wilderness AT tires after tread separations were linked to crashes involving Ford Explorer vehicles.
candidates.lesson: A component failure can become a vehicle-system failure when tire construction, operating pressure, heat, loading, handling and field data are not treated together.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Strong automotive failure candidate with official recall/investigation documentation.

candidates.title: Machhu Dam II fails after overtopping
candidates.summary: Machhu Dam II in Gujarat failed after flood inflow exceeded the dam's ability to pass water, overtopping the earthen embankments and sending destructive flooding downstream.
candidates.lesson: Dam safety is governed by extremes. Spillway capacity, gate reliability, flood forecasting, embankment erosion and warning time must be designed for the storm that exceeds expectation.
candidates.source_label: Association of State Dam Safety Officials
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. DamFailures.org case study confirms Aug. 11, 1979, overtopping of earthen embankments and failure of Machhu Dam II.

candidates.title: The first transatlantic telegraph message crosses the ocean
candidates.summary: The first official message passed along the 1858 transatlantic telegraph cable, proving that electrical communication could link Europe and North America across the ocean.
candidates.lesson: A communications breakthrough needs the whole channel: cable manufacture, laying method, insulation, signal power, operators and repair reality all decide whether the message arrives.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. IET source confirms the first official message on Aug. 16, 1858 and notes the cable's later failure from technical problems.

candidates.title: Windows 95 puts the Start menu into everyday computing
candidates.summary: Microsoft marked the first anniversary of Windows 95 on August 24 after tens of millions of shipments. The release made the Start menu, taskbar and 32-bit consumer PC platform part of everyday use.
candidates.lesson: A consumer platform succeeds when technical architecture and interaction design arrive together: APIs, drivers, applications and a learnable interface reinforce each other.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Microsoft source supports Aug. 24 as the one-year anniversary and Windows 95 adoption/momentum.

candidates.title: Torvalds announces the Linux project
candidates.summary: Linus Torvalds first posted that he was working on Linux, beginning a collaborative kernel project that grew into major open-source infrastructure.
candidates.lesson: Software infrastructure can start small when the interfaces are open enough for others to inspect, build, repair and extend the system.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Linux Foundation source confirms Aug. 25 as the first public post/announcement date.

candidates.title: Mattmark worksite is buried by glacier ice
candidates.summary: A glacial slide from the Allalin glacier buried the Mattmark dam construction site in Valais, killing 88 workers and raising hard questions about construction siting below known alpine hazards.
candidates.lesson: Temporary works are part of the engineered system. Camps, access roads and work zones need hazard assessment with the same seriousness as the permanent structure.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Swiss source confirms Aug. 30, 1965, the Allalin glacier slide near Mattmark and 88 construction-worker deaths; useful Swiss candidate for later review.

candidates.title: Woodland and Silver patent machine-readable classification
candidates.summary: Norman Woodland and Bernard Silver received a patent for classifying articles using identifying patterns, an early barcode concept that later became essential to automated retail and logistics.
candidates.lesson: Automation often begins with identification. A machine-readable code connects physical goods to computing, inventory and process control.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Patent record confirms Oct. 7, 1952 and describes identifying patterns for article classification.

candidates.title: Windscale Pile 1 burns inside the reactor core
candidates.summary: A fire broke out in Windscale Pile 1 during a graphite-reactor annealing operation, releasing radioactive material before the reactor was cooled and brought under control.
candidates.lesson: A recovery operation is still an operating mode; stored energy, instrumentation limits and delayed feedback can turn maintenance into the accident sequence.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Useful nuclear failure entry; source supports date, fire, release and Windscale context.

candidates.title: Calder Hall opens as a full-scale nuclear power station
candidates.summary: Calder Hall was officially opened as the world's first full-scale commercial nuclear power station, connecting nuclear heat, steam generation and grid electricity as an industrial power system.
candidates.lesson: A new energy source becomes infrastructure only when reactor, balance-of-plant, grid connection, operations and public accountability all work as one system.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Good energy breakthrough; helps balance nuclear as more than accident history.

candidates.title: Cleveland's LNG tank farm explodes
candidates.summary: A liquefied-natural-gas storage tank failure at the East Ohio Gas Company triggered explosions and fires across part of Cleveland, killing more than 130 people.
candidates.lesson: Cryogenic storage is not passive. Tank geometry, material behavior, containment, vapor dispersion and urban siting all decide what happens after a leak.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Encyclopedia of Cleveland History source confirms Oct. 20, 1944, the LNG tank explosion/fire and more than 130 deaths.

candidates.title: Mercedes-Benz patents a practical automotive airbag
candidates.summary: Mercedes-Benz filed a patent for an airbag system for motor vehicles, part of the long engineering path from restraint concept to production safety equipment.
candidates.lesson: Safety innovation needs sensing, deployment timing, materials, crash data and manufacturability before a promising concept can protect people at speed.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Good automotive breakthrough; source supports the October 23, 1971 patent milestone.

candidates.title: Nedelin disaster: an R-16 explodes on the pad
candidates.summary: During rushed prelaunch work at Baikonur, a fueled Soviet R-16 missile exploded on the launch pad after premature second-stage ignition, killing many engineers and military personnel.
candidates.lesson: Do not troubleshoot a fueled high-energy system as if it were inert. Schedule pressure must never move people inside the blast radius without hard isolation.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NASA's Rockets and People series includes Chertok's account; a later source-quality pass should cite the exact volume/page if promoted.

candidates.title: Erie Canal opens a new inland route
candidates.summary: The Erie Canal was completed, connecting Lake Erie with the Hudson River through a long artificial waterway that transformed transport, trade and settlement patterns.
candidates.lesson: Infrastructure can redraw economics when route, locks, water supply, maintenance and operating rules lower friction across an entire network.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. GovInfo source confirms Oct. 26, 1825 completion, 363-mile length and transport impact.

candidates.title: Schweizerhalle fire contaminates the Rhine
candidates.summary: A fire at the Sandoz chemical warehouse in Schweizerhalle near Basel caused contaminated firefighting water to enter the Rhine, producing serious ecological damage and prompting stronger Swiss major-accident prevention rules.
candidates.lesson: Emergency response water can become a transport system for hazards; containment, drainage, storage layout and runoff paths need to be engineered before the fire.
candidates.source_label: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. FOEN/BAFU source confirms the Nov. 1, 1986 Schweizerhalle fire, ecological damage along the Rhine and later Swiss accident-prevention regulation.

candidates.title: The Morris worm slows the young internet
candidates.summary: The Morris worm spread through networked Unix systems, disrupting a significant fraction of the early internet and becoming one of the first major internet-scale security incidents.
candidates.lesson: Connectivity multiplies software risk; authentication flaws, default trust and uncontrolled replication can turn a local bug into a system-wide outage.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Strong software/systems failure candidate with official retrospective source.

candidates.title: Fundao tailings dam fails in a liquefaction flowslide
candidates.summary: The Fundao tailings dam at Samarco's Germano complex failed, releasing mine tailings downstream and killing 19 people.
candidates.lesson: Tailings storage is active infrastructure. Drainage, liquefaction risk, raising history, monitoring and emergency planning must be managed for the life of the waste.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Review Panel source confirms Nov. 5, 2015 failure and identifies liquefaction flowslide at the left abutment.

candidates.title: Edmund Fitzgerald sinks in a Lake Superior storm
candidates.summary: The freighter Edmund Fitzgerald sank during a severe Lake Superior storm with all 29 crew lost, leaving investigators to weigh weather, flooding, buoyancy and structural questions.
candidates.lesson: Marine safety depends on reserve margin under real weather: hatch integrity, freeboard, loading, routing and warning decisions must survive the worst water the vessel will meet.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms Nov. 10, 1975, Lake Superior sinking and 29 crew deaths; later pass could replace or supplement with USCG/NTSB report.

candidates.title: London's Great Smog turns air pollution lethal
candidates.summary: A cold, windless period trapped coal smoke and pollutants over London from 5 to 9 December, reducing visibility and causing a severe public-health disaster.
candidates.lesson: Environmental failures are engineered through systems too: fuel choice, emissions, weather, monitoring, public warnings and regulation decide whether pollution becomes catastrophe.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source confirms Dec. 5-9, 1952 and the severe pollution/death toll context.

candidates.title: Halifax harbour detonates after a munitions collision
candidates.summary: The explosives-laden Mont Blanc collided with Imo in Halifax harbour, caught fire and detonated, devastating nearby districts.
candidates.lesson: Hazardous cargo turns routing, signalling, firefighting distance and public exclusion zones into one life-safety system.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Canadian War Museum source confirms Dec. 6, 1917, the collision, fire and explosion of Mont Blanc's cargo.

candidates.title: Apollo 8 enters lunar orbit
candidates.summary: Apollo 8 became the first crewed mission to enter lunar orbit, giving astronauts and mission control the first human operating experience around another world.
candidates.lesson: A mission milestone is an interface test: navigation, propulsion, communications, life support and return planning must all work when Earth is no longer the operating center.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NASA source confirms Apollo 8 entered lunar orbit on Dec. 24, 1968 and describes the Christmas Eve broadcast from lunar orbit.

candidates.title: Tay Bridge collapses in a storm with a train aboard
candidates.summary: The first Tay Rail Bridge collapsed during a violent storm while a passenger train crossed its high girders. The inquiry blamed the bridge design, and the replacement raised British bridge-building standards.
candidates.lesson: Wind is a structural load. Design changes, bracing details, casting quality, inspection and operating limits must be treated as safety-critical, not secondary cost items.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Network Rail source confirms Dec. 28, 1879, storm collapse, inquiry blame on design and later higher bridge-building standards.

candidates.title: Iroquois Theatre proves fireproof claims hollow
candidates.summary: A fire at Chicago's Iroquois Theatre killed hundreds of people after stage materials ignited and escape routes failed under crowd pressure.
candidates.lesson: Life safety depends on verified details, not advertised labels: curtains, exits, doors, alarms, suppression and staff procedures must all work in the first minutes.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NFPA archive record confirms Dec. 30, 1903 investigation material; later promotion should use the full report or another detailed institutional source for exact casualty/mechanism wording.

candidates.title: Deep Impact launches toward a comet collision
candidates.summary: NASA launched Deep Impact toward comet Tempel 1, carrying an impactor and a flyby spacecraft designed to expose and observe material beneath the comet's surface.
candidates.lesson: A deliberate collision can become a precision instrument when navigation, timing, imaging and separation are engineered as one experiment.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NASA mission material supports the Jan. 12, 2005 launch and the impactor/flyby architecture; verify the exact wording during promotion.

candidates.title: USS Enterprise flight-deck fire spreads through armed aircraft
candidates.summary: A rocket detonated on the flight deck of USS Enterprise near Hawaii, igniting fuel and munitions and causing a chain of explosions that killed 28 sailors.
candidates.lesson: Stored energy turns proximity into escalation; ordnance spacing, thermal protection, firefighting access and crew training must limit one ignition from becoming many.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Institutional source selected; confirm URL accessibility and the casualty/mechanism wording before promotion.

candidates.title: ENIAC is unveiled as a general-purpose electronic computer
candidates.summary: The University of Pennsylvania publicly unveiled ENIAC, a room-sized electronic computer that used thousands of vacuum tubes to calculate far faster than electromechanical machines.
candidates.lesson: Computing scale depends on the whole machine: logic, memory, input, programming, cooling, power and maintainability must advance together.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Penn's institutional history supports the February 1946 unveiling and ENIAC's technical significance; recheck whether Feb. 14 or Feb. 15 is the best display date before promotion.

candidates.title: The prototype Spitfire makes its first flight
candidates.summary: The Supermarine Type 300 prototype that became the Spitfire made its first flight from Eastleigh, combining a stressed-skin airframe, elliptical wing and Rolls-Royce engine.
candidates.lesson: Performance emerges from integration: aerodynamics, structure, propulsion, controls and manufacturability have to improve as one aircraft.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Manufacturer heritage source supports the Mar. 5, 1936 first flight and design lineage; verify technical phrasing before promotion.

candidates.title: L'Ambiance Plaza collapses during lift-slab construction
candidates.summary: The partially built L'Ambiance Plaza apartment project in Bridgeport, Connecticut, collapsed while floor slabs were being lifted into position, killing 28 construction workers.
candidates.lesson: Temporary construction states can govern safety; connections, sequencing, bracing, load paths and communication must be designed for every stage, not only the finished building.
candidates.source_label: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NIST investigation is the preferred technical source; confirm page availability and exact collapse sequence before promotion.

candidates.title: PEPCON fire escalates through ammonium perchlorate storage
candidates.summary: A fire at the PEPCON rocket-fuel oxidizer plant in Henderson, Nevada, escalated into multiple explosions as large quantities of ammonium perchlorate became involved.
candidates.lesson: Inventory is stored consequence; segregation, siting, firewater, process isolation and emergency distance must reflect the full energetic material on site.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. USGS report documents seismic observations from the May 4, 1988 explosions; pair with the fire investigation during promotion for detailed causal wording.

candidates.title: Tazreen factory fire exposes deadly workplace escape failures
candidates.summary: A fire at the Tazreen Fashions garment factory in Bangladesh killed 112 workers and became a catalyst for national action on factory fire and building safety.
candidates.lesson: Fire protection fails when workers cannot leave; alarms, protected exits, unlocked routes, occupancy controls and credible inspection must work together.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. ILO chronology confirms Nov. 24, 2012 and 112 deaths; a promotion pass should add a detailed investigation source for specific escape-route mechanisms.

candidates.title: Atlantis launches on the final Space Shuttle mission
candidates.summary: Space Shuttle Atlantis launched on STS-135, the 135th and final mission of the Shuttle program, carrying supplies and a logistics module to the International Space Station.
candidates.lesson: A program's final flight is still an engineering mission; mature hardware depends on disciplined operations, configuration control and knowledge carried by people.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NASA mission material supports the Jul. 8, 2011 launch and final-Shuttle-program status.

candidates.title: USS Forrestal fire exposes cascading flight-deck hazards
candidates.summary: A rocket accidentally fired across USS Forrestal's flight deck, striking a fueled aircraft and starting a fire in which bombs detonated, killing 134 sailors.
candidates.lesson: High-tempo operations need barriers against accidental activation and escalation; connector design, ordnance condition, deck layout and firefighting readiness all matter.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Naval History source selected for the Jul. 29, 1967 event; confirm current URL and exact initiation details before promotion.

candidates.title: The San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge opens
candidates.summary: The original San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge opened to traffic, linking the cities with a complex crossing of suspension spans, a tunnel and a cantilever section.
candidates.lesson: A megaproject succeeds by joining distinct structures into one transport system: foundations, spans, tunnel, approaches and operations must share compatible assumptions.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Caltrans is the preferred institutional source; confirm that the linked history page exposes the Nov. 12, 1936 opening before promotion.

candidates.title: Edison receives a patent for recording sound
candidates.summary: Thomas Edison received a U.S. patent for the phonograph, describing a machine that could record vibrations from speech or other sounds and reproduce them later.
candidates.lesson: A new medium begins with a transducer: capture physical motion, preserve it in a repeatable form and convert it back into something people can perceive.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Patent record confirms Feb. 19, 1878 and describes recording and reproducing sounds; strong primary-source candidate.

candidates.title: Flight 981 crashes after an explosive cargo-door failure
candidates.summary: Turkish Airlines Flight 981 crashed after its DC-10 rear cargo door opened in flight, causing decompression, floor collapse and loss of critical control cables.
candidates.lesson: A warning is not a barrier. Latch geometry, indication, structural load paths and control routing must prevent one closure error from disabling the aircraft.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. FAA Lessons Learned supports the Mar. 3, 1974 event and cargo-door/decompression sequence.

candidates.title: Maxwell demonstrates additive colour photography
candidates.summary: James Clerk Maxwell presented a colour image made from three separate red, green and blue photographic records, demonstrating the principle behind additive colour imaging.
candidates.lesson: Complex colour can be reconstructed from a few controlled channels; measurement, filtering, registration and projection turn theory into a visible system.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Science Museum Group collection documents the tartan-ribbon experiment; verify the May 17 presentation date against the Royal Institution record before promotion.

candidates.title: Baia Mare tailings spill sends cyanide into rivers
candidates.summary: A tailings containment failure near Baia Mare, Romania, released cyanide-contaminated water into the river system, causing extensive transboundary ecological damage.
candidates.lesson: Waste containment must be designed for weather, water balance and downstream consequence; a process boundary does not stop at a national border.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. UNEP assessment is the preferred source for the Jan. 30, 2000 spill; verify release quantities and failure mechanism during promotion.

candidates.title: Mechanically sliced bread reaches customers
candidates.summary: The Chillicothe Baking Company began selling bread sliced by Otto Rohwedder's machine, pairing uniform cutting with packaging that kept the loaf together.
candidates.lesson: Food automation succeeds when the machine and the product meet: cutting speed, slice consistency, handling and packaging must preserve quality through sale.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Smithsonian supports the Jul. 7, 1928 Chillicothe debut; useful candidate in the underrepresented food-engineering category.

candidates.title: The Jazz Singer synchronizes recorded sound with cinema
candidates.summary: The Jazz Singer premiered using the Vitaphone sound-on-disc system, helping move commercial cinema from silent projection toward synchronized dialogue and music.
candidates.lesson: Synchronization is an interface problem: recording, playback speed, projection, amplification and distribution must stay aligned for the illusion to work.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Library of Congress essay supports the film's 1927 release and Vitaphone significance; confirm the Oct. 6 premiere date during promotion.

candidates.title: Prestige suffers hull damage with 77,000 tonnes of fuel aboard
candidates.summary: The single-hull tanker Prestige suffered hull damage in heavy seas off Galicia while carrying about 77,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil, beginning a prolonged maritime pollution disaster.
candidates.lesson: A damaged ship becomes a regional systems problem; structural condition, cargo, weather, towage and access to refuge determine whether a casualty can be contained.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. European Commission document confirms Nov. 13, 2002, single-hull construction, heavy weather and cargo quantity.

candidates.title: Lunokhod 1 becomes the first rover on another world
candidates.summary: Luna 17 landed on the Moon and deployed Lunokhod 1, the first successful remotely controlled rover to operate on another celestial body.
candidates.lesson: Remote mobility combines vehicle mechanics with delayed human control; traction, power, thermal survival, cameras and communications must close the loop.
candidates.source_label: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Smithsonian confirms Nov. 17, 1970 and the first remote-controlled lunar rover claim.

candidates.title: Enschede fireworks depot explodes inside a residential district
candidates.summary: A fire at the S.E. Fireworks storage complex in Enschede escalated into massive explosions, killing 23 people and devastating the surrounding neighborhood.
candidates.lesson: Hazard classification, inventory control and land-use planning are one safety system; paperwork cannot make energetic material compatible with nearby homes.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Event/date are well established, but this landing page is too generic; promotion requires the Dutch inquiry or another event-specific government source.

candidates.title: Dupont Plaza Hotel fire races through public spaces
candidates.summary: A deliberately set fire spread rapidly through the lobby and casino of the Dupont Plaza Hotel in San Juan, killing 98 people.
candidates.lesson: Buildings must remain survivable even when ignition is deliberate; sprinklers, compartmentation, exits, alarms, finishes and evacuation management provide independent layers.
candidates.source_label: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NIST confirms Dec. 31, 1986, rapid spread and 98 deaths; strong institutional source.

candidates.title: ARPANET switches to TCP/IP
candidates.summary: ARPANET hosts moved from NCP to TCP/IP in a planned flag-day transition, helping turn separate packet networks into the interoperable foundation of the modern internet.
candidates.lesson: A network becomes infrastructure when interfaces are standardized; protocol migration, timing and backward-compatibility planning matter as much as the protocol itself.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source supports the Jan. 1, 1983 ARPANET NCP-to-TCP/IP flag-day transition and its role in internet interoperability.

candidates.title: Tasman Bridge collapses after a ship strike
candidates.summary: The bulk carrier Lake Illawarra struck the Tasman Bridge in Hobart, collapsing two piers and 127 metres of bridge deck. Twelve people died, including motorists who drove into the gap.
candidates.lesson: Bridge risk is not only vertical load; navigation channels, pier protection, traffic control and night visibility must be part of the safety case.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Source supports Jan. 5, 1975, Lake Illawarra collision, collapsed piers/decking and casualty details.

candidates.title: Mariner 10 makes the first Mercury flyby
candidates.summary: NASA's Mariner 10 flew past Mercury at close range, returning the first spacecraft measurements and images from the innermost planet.
candidates.lesson: A flyby is a brief systems exam: navigation, pointing, instruments, power and communications must all work during the few minutes when the science is possible.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NASA source supports the Mar. 29, 1974 closest encounter and Mercury measurements; promotion pass should refine image/measurement wording.

candidates.title: USS Iowa's turret explodes during a firing exercise
candidates.summary: A rapid series of explosions inside Turret II aboard USS Iowa killed 47 sailors during a gunnery exercise, triggering Navy and later independent technical investigations.
candidates.lesson: Legacy weapon systems still need modern process discipline; propellant handling, loading sequence, instrumentation and investigation independence all matter when stored energy is immense.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. NHHC source supports Apr. 19, 1989, Turret II explosions and 47 deaths; promotion should keep cause wording careful because investigations differed.

candidates.title: Mariner 4 returns the first close-up views of Mars
candidates.summary: Mariner 4 made its closest approach to Mars and captured the first close-up images of another planet, replacing speculation with direct spacecraft observations.
candidates.lesson: Exploration changes when instruments cross the distance: navigation, imaging, storage and deep-space communication turn a flyby into evidence.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. JPL source supports the Jul. 14, 1965 closest approach and first photos of another planet from space.

candidates.title: Saudia 163 lands but never evacuates
candidates.summary: Saudi Arabian Airlines Flight 163 returned to Riyadh after an in-flight fire warning, but the aircraft stopped without an immediate evacuation and all 301 people aboard died.
candidates.lesson: Survival after landing depends on the emergency sequence: detection, decision, shutdown, door operation, cabin crew action and rescue access all have to happen fast.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. FAA Lessons Learned source supports Aug. 19, 1980, the in-flight fire, return to Riyadh and evacuation failure context.

candidates.title: AeroMexico 498 collides in busy terminal airspace
candidates.summary: AeroMexico Flight 498 and a private Piper collided over Cerritos, California, exposing limits in see-and-avoid, transponder coverage and terminal-area traffic protection.
candidates.lesson: Airspace safety needs engineered visibility: surveillance, altitude reporting, collision alerts and clear responsibility must cover the traffic mix actually present.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. FAA Lessons Learned source supports the Aug. 31, 1986 midair collision and the safety-system context.

candidates.title: Carlson makes the first xerographic image
candidates.summary: Chester Carlson and Otto Kornei produced the first xerographic image, proving that electrostatic copying could capture and reproduce marks without wet photographic chemistry.
candidates.lesson: A useful office machine begins as a materials-and-fields problem: charge, exposure, powder adhesion and transfer have to become a repeatable process.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. Xerox source supports the Oct. 22, 1938 first xerographic image text and the later copier lineage.

candidates.title: Singapore 006 starts takeoff on a closed runway
candidates.summary: Singapore Airlines Flight 006 attempted takeoff from the wrong runway at Taipei during typhoon conditions and struck construction equipment, destroying the aircraft.
candidates.lesson: Runway safety is an interface system: signage, lighting, charts, clearance, surface surveillance and crew position awareness must agree in low visibility.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. TTSB page supports Oct. 31, 2000, wrong-runway takeoff attempt, typhoon conditions and construction-equipment impact.

candidates.title: Bell Labs gets semiconductor amplification
candidates.summary: John Bardeen and Walter Brattain's point-contact device produced semiconductor amplification, an experimental result that led directly to the transistor.
candidates.lesson: A device breakthrough often arrives as a measurable effect first; packaging, theory, manufacturing and reliability then turn the effect into a platform.
candidates.notes: Free-date candidate. CHM source supports Dec. 16, 1947 as the first successful semiconductor amplifier and the later Dec. 23 demonstration to Bell Labs officials.

candidates.title: The A-4/V-2 rocket makes its first successful flight
candidates.summary: A German A-4/V-2 test launch from Peenemunde became the first successful flight of a large liquid-fueled ballistic rocket, proving technologies later reused in space launch vehicles.
candidates.lesson: Engineering progress can come from morally compromised systems; technical lessons should be separated from celebration and carried forward with historical honesty.
candidates.source_label: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
candidates.notes: October candidate. Source supports the Oct. 3, 1942 first successful flight. Promotion should keep the wording sober because the V-2 was a weapon built in a coercive wartime system.

candidates.title: USS Holland enters U.S. Navy submarine service
candidates.summary: The U.S. Navy commissioned Holland, a compact submarine with gasoline engine surface propulsion, electric submerged propulsion and torpedo armament, marking the start of U.S. submarine service.
candidates.lesson: A new vehicle class becomes real when propulsion, controls, weapons, crew operation and maintenance are accepted into regular service.
candidates.notes: October candidate. NHHC source supports the Oct. 12, 1900 commissioning and basic vessel identity.

candidates.title: Ether anesthesia is demonstrated in surgery
candidates.summary: At Massachusetts General Hospital's Ether Dome, William Morton administered ether while John Collins Warren removed a tumor, demonstrating that surgery could be performed without the usual pain.
candidates.lesson: A medical breakthrough needs delivery control, observation and repeatable procedure; the active substance alone is not the whole system.
candidates.notes: October candidate. Source supports Oct. 16, 1846 and the successful public ether demonstration at Massachusetts General Hospital; a Mass General primary page would be preferable if found later.

candidates.title: USS Tang is sunk by its own torpedo
candidates.summary: USS Tang was lost after one of its torpedoes malfunctioned, circled back and struck the submarine. Only nine crew members survived.
candidates.lesson: A weapon is still part of the launching platform's safety case; guidance, arming logic and post-launch behavior must be considered as hazards to the operator too.
candidates.notes: October candidate. NHHC source selected for Tang's final patrol and loss; promotion should verify exact circular-run wording from the page or an official patrol report.

candidates.title: Baku Metro fire traps passengers underground
candidates.summary: A fire on a Baku Metro train between stations killed hundreds of passengers and exposed the extreme evacuation difficulty of smoke, toxic gases and stalled trains in tunnels.
candidates.lesson: Tunnel transport safety depends on evacuation time: materials, ventilation, emergency lighting, communication and train control have to preserve survivable escape paths.
candidates.notes: October candidate. Event is a strong fire-safety candidate for Oct. 28, but source is institutional/secondary rather than official; promotion should look for an inquiry or standards-body source.

candidates.title: Boeing Model 299 crashes and exposes cockpit complexity
candidates.summary: The Boeing Model 299 prototype crashed during takeoff at Wright Field after the elevator controls remained locked, a failure later associated with the adoption of formal cockpit checklists.
candidates.lesson: When a machine becomes too complex to remember safely, the interface must include procedure: checklists turn fragile memory into engineered operation.
candidates.source_label: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
candidates.notes: October candidate. Smithsonian source supports the 1935 Model 299 crash and checklist significance; promotion should verify exact Oct. 30 date against an accident record.
